title: Watermark an AI-designed protein
description: A design model writes a faint, key-detectable pattern into a protein's amino-acid sequence and into its predicted 3D shape. Substitutions are kept only when the protein still folds and binds, so the watermarked binder works like the unmarked one. A lab or a DNA foundry with the detection key can tell the protein was designed by a model.
body: In lab tests, watermarked binders matched unmarked designs on hit rate and binding strength, and kept a similar spread of sequences. The mark is provenance for biosecurity screening and for open protein databases, separating model-made designs from natural ones. It is not permanent. Running the same fold through a different design tool can yield a new sequence that keeps the function and drops the mark.
